response.markdown_report:
The next experiment should verify the exported BERT4Rec predictor against the trained in-memory model before changing its learning objective. At 20% progress, this closes an actionable verification gap without training another predictor.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** First, all 14,148 audited supervision positions contained MASK, but original corruption provenance was unavailable. Mask presence therefore cannot establish correct event alignment or loss wiring. Second, recent-content substitution damaged training-prefix recovery more than block swaps. This supports content dependence under those interventions, without establishing causal recency or held-out usefulness. Third, 800 live identity checks passed, while fresh-process predictor parity remained unavailable. Repeating an in-memory computation cannot verify exported preprocessing, routing or checkpoint selection.

**Insights from related work.** BERT4Rec reconstructs masked items, and RecTools reserves an appended mask for prediction [1,2]. These semantics give concrete assertions for target hiding and absolute readout position. PyTorch documents evaluation-mode requirements, while TensorFlow discusses shared preprocessing to reduce training-serving skew [3,4]. Consequently, parity must exercise the exported entry point and its actual transformations. PCGrad provides a framework for conflicting task gradients [5]. Interior-versus-terminal gradient comparisons could motivate later objective experiments, but would not demonstrate generalization gains.

The resulting framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Production integrity | Consumed-event and same-forward loss replay | Bounded captures miss other paths |
| Deployment consistency | Exported inputs, scores, rankings and manifests | Shared implementation errors can survive |
| Objective alignment | Interior/terminal losses and gradient cosine | Local conflict does not imply poor HR@10 |

Three atomic ideas follow; scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exported-predictor parity audit [1–4] | 4/8/5 | Connects semantic fixtures with actual deployment artifacts | Integration contribution; requires a reload runner |
| Consumed-event replay | 4/7/6 | Checks exact supervision and loss inputs | Substantial transport work; finite coverage |
| Interior/terminal gradient probe [1,5] | 5/7/6 | Can localize objective disagreement | Additional backward passes; indirect ranking evidence |

**Selected algorithm.** Fix a small public-history fixture panel before execution, covering all four routes, unequal left padding, repeated items, empty histories and truncation boundaries. Compare canonical IDs, appended-mask location, greatest nonpadding readout, candidate-aligned scores and tie-aware rankings between the live model and the actual exported predictor. Verify mapping, configuration and checkpoint manifests; calibrate assertions with independently verified faults and harmless batch/candidate permutations.

Report assertion denominators, discrepancies, false alarms and unavailable checks. Preserve one checkpoint per category and all diagnostic interfaces. Passing this audit establishes bounded deployment consistency; only the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 selects revisions. No accuracy improvement is claimed.

idea.description: Add a bounded, fault-calibrated audit comparing the actual exported working/predict.py path with the corresponding live BERT4Rec category model, including canonical inputs, artifact identity, candidate scores and rankings.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics report successful live identity checks but explicitly lack fresh-process predictor parity. A wrong item mapping, category route, checkpoint, mask construction or left-padding readout could invalidate deployment despite correct live scores. This audit addresses that uncertainty before spending the shared budget on objective changes.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is an integration specification, not executable replacement training code: the actual trainer, predictor writer and reload interface were not supplied. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView interfaces. Add an optional host-supported exported-predictor runner; absent that runner, return null with an explicit reason rather than certifying parity. Exercise the actual generated predictor and its normal checkpoint loading, preprocessing and category routing. A diagnostic runner may observe internal inputs, but must not replace the exported preprocessing with audit preprocessing.

Predeclare a bounded fixture panel using only supplied training histories and catalog mappings. Cover the four categories, empty and short histories, repeated IDs, unequal left padding, near-limit histories and truncation. Empty-history behavior must follow the supplied baseline; unsupported behavior is reported explicitly. Independently construct expected left-padded tokens using the last L-1 events followed by the reserved MASK. Verify the greatest nonpadding absolute position, never count-1. Do not assert arbitrary padding-shift invariance when absolute positions change.

Fix candidate IDs and ordering before comparisons; exclude PAD and MASK from candidates. Compare exact canonical inputs first, then finite candidate-aligned logits with predeclared dtype/device-specific tolerances. Define deterministic tie handling; report raw rank differences and score gaps, distinguishing near-tie numerical differences from clear order reversals. Do not silently relax tolerance after failures. Compare singleton versus batched calls, repeated calls, consistently reordered batch rows and candidate permutations inverted before comparison.

Persist a trial-local manifest containing category, architecture configuration, item-map digest, special-token IDs and selected checkpoint digest. Compare observed exported artifacts against the independently recorded training manifest. Matching digests establish artifact identity relative to that manifest, not correctness of the manifest itself.

On copied fixtures only, inject count-based readout, omitted MASK, nonidentity mapping swaps, wrong routing and incompatible artifact combinations where applicable. Independently verify that each injection changes its intended property before counting detection. Count attempted, inapplicable, invalid, equivalent, unresolved, verified-corrupt, detected and surviving cases separately. Report false alarms on independently checked clean and harmless controls. Mutants never train models or supply recommendation scores.

Preserve module modes and main-process RNG states in finally. Do not advance the production loader for parity fixtures. Keep existing family-safe diagnostics, consumed-pipeline replay and missing-data reporting. The interpreter prompt must distinguish deployment consistency, supervision integrity, training recovery and host validation. Public titles, descriptions and timestamps are allowed; unavailable ratings, review content, commercial attributes and simulator traits remain unavailable.

Retain exactly one selected independently trained BERT4Rec checkpoint per category, without averaging or additional fitted scorers. Audit comparisons are checks of the same checkpoint, not score fusion. Preserve all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per completed epoch. Preserve twenty designated training users' full-catalog unseen-item recommendations. Log audit runtime against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Only pinned host macro validation HR@10 selects revisions; no test access or held-out gain is assumed.
idea.pseudocode:
def audit_exported_predictor(view, exported_runner, training_manifest):
    if exported_runner is None:
        return unavailable('Actual exported-predictor runner not supplied')
    state = capture_module_modes_and_main_process_rng(view.model)
    try:
        view.model.eval()
        fixtures = predefined_public_training_history_panel()
        observed_manifest = exported_runner.inspect_loaded_artifacts()
        check_manifest_against_training_record(observed_manifest, training_manifest)
        with inference_mode():
            for fixture in fixtures:
                expected = independent_appended_mask_encoding(fixture)
                live = observe_live_path(view, fixture)
                deployed = exported_runner.observe_actual_entry_point(fixture)
                check_exact_tokens_mapping_route_and_readout(expected, live, deployed)
                check_finite_candidate_aligned_scores(live, deployed, fixed_tolerances)
                report_tie_aware_rank_differences(live, deployed)
                for control in predefined_harmless_transformations(fixture):
                    independently_verify_control_preconditions(control)
                    check_after_inverse_alignment(control, view, exported_runner)
                for operator in predefined_fault_operators:
                    mutant, evidence = inject_into_isolated_copy(fixture, operator)
                    status = independently_verify_injection(fixture, mutant, evidence)
                    record_status_and_detector_result(status, mutant)
        return metrics_definitions_counts_failures_and_unavailable_reasons()
    finally:
        restore_module_modes_and_main_process_rng(state)

class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        result = existing_family_safe_diagnostics(train_loader)
        result.update(audit_exported_predictor(
            self.view, optional_actual_export_runner(), training_manifest()))
        return result

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return evidence_grounded_prompt(
        raw_diagnosis,
        distinguish=['deployment consistency', 'supervision integrity',
                     'training recovery', 'host validation'],
        require=['definitions', 'denominators', 'fault verification',
                 'false alarms', 'unavailable reasons'],
        constrain='one independently trained BERT4Rec checkpoint per category')

originality.positive: Combines BERT4Rec semantic assertions, exported artifact identity and verified fault calibration in the fixed RecHarness interface.
originality.negative: Differential checks, manifests and metamorphic controls are established engineering techniques; no new learning principle is introduced.

future_potential.positive: Creates a reusable gate for subsequent architecture and objective experiments, especially when predictor code is generated separately.
future_potential.negative: Bounded agreement can miss shared errors and does not directly improve ranking quality or establish immediate usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no retraining or new scoring network, and a small fixture panel bounds computation.
code_difficulty.negative: Observing the actual exported path, managing fresh-process execution and verifying injected faults require host integration.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Uses bidirectional Transformer representations and masked-item reconstruction for sequential recommendation.
Provides the architectural basis for preserving target hiding and mask-based inference.
limitations: Does not establish correctness of this task's sampler, exported predictor or checkpoint routing.
Masked reconstruction accuracy does not itself establish next-item validation performance.

related_work.title: RecTools BERT4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides concrete implementation guidance for left padding, reserving an appended mask position and prediction from that token.
limitations: A reference implementation cannot certify that the supplied production path follows the same semantics.
Absolute position embeddings preclude assuming arbitrary padding shifts preserve scores.

related_work.title: PyTorch: Saving and Loading Models
contributions: Documents checkpoint loading and the need to set evaluation mode for inference.
limitations: Successful weight loading alone does not verify category routing, item mapping or artifact identity.

related_work.title: TensorFlow Transform best practices
contributions: Motivates consistent preprocessing between training and serving.
limitations: General pipeline guidance does not supply a BERT4Rec-specific parity protocol.

related_work.title: Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
contributions: Introduces PCGrad to address conflicting gradients between training objectives.
Motivates a subsequent diagnostic comparing interior-mask and terminal-mask gradient directions.
limitations: Applying gradient comparisons to BERT4Rec is a proposed adaptation.
Negative gradient cosine alone does not demonstrate worse recommendation generalization.
